pure-announcement.rationale: Though it is a tool README, it explains transferable analysis techniques (attacker-first forward reasoning, self-falsification) that the note itself says can be adapted to other models, not just an X-is-released notice.

duplicate.rationale: No nearest concept covers agentic vulnerability discovery; OSV format and SIEM visibility are adjacent security topics, not this approach.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The tool is open-source with a public benchmarking harness against known-vulnerable corpora (NodeGoat, Juice Shop, WebGoat), so its detection claims are reproducible.

durability.rationale: The forward attacker-first-vs-sink-first analysis contrast and the self-falsification-to-cut-false-positives discipline are reasoning patterns that outlast the Opus/Claude Code plumbing and install steps that date the note.

actionability.rationale: A security engineer can adopt the entry-point-forward analysis, the disprove-your-own-finding filter, and the independent read-only verify step in their own pipeline regardless of whether they run VulnHunter.

atomicity.rationale: The note bundles several separable ideas — attacker-first forward analysis, the falsification engine, and the hunt/fix/verify loop with an independent verifier — each promotable on its own, so one paragraph cannot hold it.
